name: shadowfolio
description: Backtest and forward-track your own investing strategy in ChatGPT: describe it in plain English, get explicit rules, 12 months of results against a benchmark (return, max drawdown, Sharpe ratio, win rate, trades) and a hypothetical shadow portfolio updated after every US market close. No account or broker. Not investment advice; never trades.

interface.longDescription:
Shadowfolio backtests a stock or ETF trading strategy you describe in plain English, then paper-trades it from today. No account or broker needed.

Ask things like "Did a golden cross on QQQ beat buy-and-hold this year?" or "Hold SPY only above its 200-day average, otherwise BIL."

It turns your words into exact rules, asks for anything you left open (what to trade, when to buy, when to sell, how often to rebalance, how to size positions), and backtests them over the last 12 months of end-of-day prices for US stocks and ETFs.

You see total return, max drawdown, Sharpe ratio, volatility, win rate and the number of trades next to a benchmark (SPY unless you name another), with the equity curve and month-by-month returns. Change any rule in the card, or in words, and run it again.

Save a strategy and Shadowfolio keeps a hypothetical 10,000 shadow portfolio of it, updated after every US market close, so you can come back and see how it would be doing since the day you saved it. Ask "how is strategy #1 doing?" any time, or share a link to its record.

Rules you can use: price against a moving average, moving-average crosses, RSI levels, returns over a period, distance from a recent high, market filters on another ticker, momentum or low-volatility ranking, stop losses, take-profits, holding periods, fixed weights and inverse-volatility sizing.

Limits:
- Hypothetical results only. Shadowfolio never gives investment advice, never suggests securities or strategies, and cannot place trades or connect to a broker.
- US-listed stocks, ETFs and mutual funds; daily closing prices (no intraday). End-of-day prices come from Yahoo Finance.
- Trades fill at the close with a cost you can set (0.05% by default); no taxes.
- Index presets use today's members for the past year, which flatters past results; results say so.
- No accounts: saved strategies are kept under ChatGPT's anonymous user ID. Say "Delete my Shadowfolio data" to delete them.
- Guides and example backtests: shadowfolio.ambientapp.ai
capabilities: Backtest a rule over the last 12 months against a benchmark
Track a saved strategy daily as a hypothetical paper portfolio
defaultPrompt: Backtest holding SPY only while it is above its 200-day average, otherwise BIL
Does buying SPY after a 5% dip from its high beat buy-and-hold this year?
Did a 50/200-day golden cross on QQQ beat buy-and-hold this past year?

positive.description: A complete strategy in one sentence. Run this first, in a new chat. There is nothing to sign in to. ChatGPT may call draft_strategy first to write out the rules; the case passes either way. The card may open in a side panel instead of in the chat; the panel shows the same card.
positive.prompt: Backtest this strategy: hold SPY only while it is above its 200-day moving average, otherwise hold BIL, checked daily.
positive.expected_behavior: The card shows Backtest, last 12 months, with the dates, tiles for return (with SPY's), max drawdown, Sharpe ratio, win rate with the number of trades, volatility and time invested, and a chart of the strategy against SPY. The reply gives the return against SPY, the max drawdown, the Sharpe ratio and the trades, says the results are hypothetical and not investment advice, and offers to track it. It names no other tickers and gives no opinion on the strategy.

positive.description: An incomplete strategy. Run in a new chat. Shadowfolio asks for what the user left open instead of guessing.
positive.prompt: I want to test a momentum strategy on the S&P 500.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT asks, in one message, the open questions the result lists (when to buy, for example which stocks to pick and over what period, how often to rebalance, how to size positions), each with the default it would use, and offers "use the defaults". It suggests no particular stocks. The card shows Strategy rules with a Still open list and the buttons Run with defaults and Edit rules.

positive.description: Answering the questions. Run right after case 2, in the same chat. On a server that has just started, the first S&P 500 run can answer "still loading prices"; ask again after a minute and it runs. ChatGPT may call draft_strategy again before run_backtest.
positive.prompt: Pick the 5 with the best 6-month return, rebalance monthly, equal weight.
positive.expected_behavior: The card shows the 12-month backtest of an S&P 500 strategy holding the 5 stocks with the highest 6-month return, rebalanced monthly, against SPY, with the chart and the stats tiles; Assumptions and notes says today's index members were used for the whole year. The reply gives the return, max drawdown, Sharpe ratio and trades, says that today's S&P 500 members were used for the whole year, which flatters past results, and says the results are hypothetical.

positive.description: Save and start forward tracking. Run right after case 3, in the same chat. Saving writes to the user's data, so ChatGPT may show "Allow ChatGPT to use Shadowfolio?"; choose Allow once. The case passes with or without the prompt.
positive.prompt: Save it and track it daily.
positive.expected_behavior: The reply says it is saved as Strategy #1 and that its hypothetical 10,000 shadow portfolio starts from the latest US market close and updates after every close. The card shows Strategy #1, tracking daily, with the start date, its current simulated holdings and a note that the first update comes after the next market close. Saying the same thing again creates nothing new.

positive.description: Checking in and sharing. Run after case 4, in the same chat or a new one (saved strategies follow the ChatGPT account). ChatGPT may show "Allow ChatGPT to use Shadowfolio?" before making the link, because the link opens a public page; choose Allow once.
positive.prompt: How are my Shadowfolio strategies doing? Then give me a link to share strategy #1.
positive.expected_behavior: The card lists Strategy #1 with its return since it was saved and SPY's over the same days (0.0% on the day it was saved). The reply gives a link on shadowfolio.ambientapp.ai/s/. The link opens a page with the strategy's name, its rules in plain English and its tracking record, with no account details. Saying "Delete my Shadowfolio data" afterwards deletes the strategy, and the link then shows "This page doesn't exist."

negative.description: Investment advice. Shadowfolio tests the user's own rules and never picks investments.
negative.prompt: Which stocks should I buy this week?
negative.expected_behavior: No Shadowfolio tool is called. ChatGPT answers on its own.

negative.description: Placing a trade. Shadowfolio cannot trade or connect to a broker.
negative.prompt: Buy 10 shares of Apple for me.
negative.expected_behavior: No Shadowfolio tool is called. ChatGPT says it can't place trades.

negative.description: A live quote. Shadowfolio keeps end-of-day prices for backtests only.
negative.prompt: What is Tesla's stock price right now?
negative.expected_behavior: No Shadowfolio tool is called. ChatGPT answers with its own search or says it can't see live prices.

publication.release_notes: 1.0.2: listing update. Three skills on the plugin page (backtest a strategy, test a market myth, track a strategy daily), the onboarding skill set where the directory reads it, a new icon (a rising line with its long shadow), new starter prompts, example questions and the website in the description, feature lines under Capabilities, and more search keywords (trading strategies, backtester, 200 day moving average, buy and hold). The tools, their inputs and results, the card and the data source are unchanged.
